title: Ordering equivalence is proven across the derived plan chain
statement: Capability 007 must prove that equivalent normalized inputs and equivalent representations of one activation plan produce byte-identical canonical plan bodies, equal domain-separated digests, and identical decode outcomes and diagnostic ordering regardless of source document order, and that the accepted Python compiler and accepted C++ decoder agree on that one canonical body and digest.
applicability: X-Verse capability 007 phase 4 XDL-derived activation-plan chain; bounded committed fixtures and repository-owned synthetic vectors.
verification_intent: Refined by T020-SR-001 and T020-SR-005; verified by the T20OrderingEquivalence CTest cases and the T020 pytest ordering cases.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: member-reordered, whitespace-varied, and integral-number-variant representations of one plan yield one canonical byte string and one digest from both the Python reference and the C++ decoder.
AC-2: per-collection ordering by the declared key, unique keys, and the duplicate-free activationOrder rule are asserted; an out-of-order or duplicate-keyed collection is rejected.
AC-3: diagnostics are ordered deterministically and a reordered-but-equivalent input yields the same decoded diagnostics and outcome.
